q: What is watchman's tour equipment for?
o: Recording that guards visit set points on their rounds
ref: Security and signal system terminology (Grondzik and Kwok); Fire Code of the Philippines (RA 9514)
n: Guards check in at stations on their route. Some systems also let them call in or raise an alarm.

q: What does a sprinkler waterflow switch do?
o: Measures the building's water use for billing
Senses water flowing in sprinkler pipe and sets off the fire alarm
ref: Security and signal system terminology (Grondzik and Kwok); Fire Code of the Philippines (RA 9514)
n: Flow means a head has opened, so the alarm sounds and the fire department is called.

q: What does a general alarm key switch do?
o: Lets authorized staff sound the building-wide alarm
ref: Security and signal system terminology (Grondzik and Kwok); Fire Code of the Philippines (RA 9514)
n: The key keeps the public from setting off a general alarm.

q: What does door or exit control hardware do?
o: Signals when a controlled door is opened without authorization
ref: Security and signal system terminology (Grondzik and Kwok); Fire Code of the Philippines (RA 9514)
n: Exit alarms on emergency doors deter misuse while keeping them usable.

q: Why must electronic locks on exit doors be coordinated with fire safety?
o: So security never blocks required escape in an emergency
So doors stay locked during fires
ref: Security and signal system terminology (Grondzik and Kwok); Fire Code of the Philippines (RA 9514)
n: Locks on egress doors must release on fire alarm or power failure.

q: What does a card reader do?
o: Reads an access card to let authorized people in
ref: Security and signal system terminology (Grondzik and Kwok); Fire Code of the Philippines (RA 9514)
n: Access control levels: card alone; card plus PIN; card checked by a guard against the person's photo.

q: How do door and window contacts detect intrusion?
o: A magnet and switch open the circuit when the door or window opens
A microphone hears the fire alarm
ref: Security and signal system terminology (Grondzik and Kwok); Fire Code of the Philippines (RA 9514)
n: Contacts are the most common perimeter intrusion devices.

q: What is the second level of access control security?
o: A guard comparing the card photo with the person
ref: Security and signal system terminology (Grondzik and Kwok); Fire Code of the Philippines (RA 9514)
n: Access control levels: card alone; card plus PIN; card checked by a guard against the person's photo.

q: How is breaking glass detected?
o: By acoustic, vibration or glass-break sensors
ref: Security and signal system terminology (Grondzik and Kwok); Fire Code of the Philippines (RA 9514)
n: Glass-break sensors listen for the sound pattern of breaking glass.

q: Why is a card plus a PIN more secure than a card alone?
o: It needs something you have and something you know
ref: Security and signal system terminology (Grondzik and Kwok); Fire Code of the Philippines (RA 9514)
n: A stolen card is useless without the PIN.

q: How do intrusion systems differ from fire alarm systems?
o: They sense heat and smoke only
They sense entry and movement, not heat, smoke or flame
ref: Security and signal system terminology (Grondzik and Kwok); Fire Code of the Philippines (RA 9514)
n: Both use initiating devices, a control panel and signals, but for different threats.

q: What can a guard do from a watchman's tour station?
o: Open every door in the building
Call in by intercom or send an alarm
ref: Security and signal system terminology (Grondzik and Kwok); Fire Code of the Philippines (RA 9514)
n: Call-in lets the control desk know the guard is safe.

q: Where are sprinkler waterflow signals shown?
o: On the sprinkler annunciator or fire alarm panel
ref: Security and signal system terminology (Grondzik and Kwok); Fire Code of the Philippines (RA 9514)
n: The panel shows which zone is flowing.

q: What else is monitored on a sprinkler system besides waterflow?
o: Valve tamper switches, so a closed valve shows as trouble
ref: Security and signal system terminology (Grondzik and Kwok); Fire Code of the Philippines (RA 9514)
n: A shut valve would leave the system dead, so valves are supervised.

q: Which doors typically get door or exit control?
o: Exterior doors and doors to restricted areas
ref: Security and signal system terminology (Grondzik and Kwok); Fire Code of the Philippines (RA 9514)
n: Control is placed where entry must be limited or watched.

q: What does an intrusion detection system detect?
ref: Security and signal system terminology (Grondzik and Kwok); Fire Code of the Philippines (RA 9514)
n: Intrusion devices include contacts, motion sensors, beams and glass-break sensors.

q: What is the first (lowest) level of access control?
o: A guard checking the card photo
ref: Security and signal system terminology (Grondzik and Kwok); Fire Code of the Philippines (RA 9514)
n: Access control levels: card alone; card plus PIN; card checked by a guard against the person's photo.

q: What is metallic foil tape on windows used for?
o: Breaking a circuit to set off an alarm when the glass breaks
ref: Security and signal system terminology (Grondzik and Kwok); Fire Code of the Philippines (RA 9514)
n: Foil tape is an older intrusion method; glass-break sensors replaced it.

q: What is the third (highest) level of access control?
o: A guard compares the card holder with the photo and records
No card, only a guest book
ref: Security and signal system terminology (Grondzik and Kwok); Fire Code of the Philippines (RA 9514)
n: Access control levels: card alone; card plus PIN; card checked by a guard against the person's photo.

q: How does a beam-interruption detector work?
o: It senses smoke in a chamber
It melts at a set temperature
An infrared beam between two points is broken by someone passing
ref: Security and signal system terminology (Grondzik and Kwok); Fire Code of the Philippines (RA 9514)
n: Beams guard long corridors, fences and openings.
